title: Ingest, assemble, validate and pinflow for new open LLM artifacts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: implement an end-to-end intake pipeline that takes community-published model weights (HF/OSS bundles), converts them to Redwood runtime artifacts, runs deterministic validation and safety checks, generates a performance profile (latency/cost/quality), and emits a recommended pin (model version + runtime config) into the model catalog.

Scope: weights ingestion, format normalization, quantization pass (optional per profile), deterministic unit tests, evicted-token regression checks, runtime microbench profiling across representative sequence lengths & batch sizes, compatibility matrix generation, and automated pin suggestion with metadata for Console consumption. This ticket covers engineering for the orchestration and validation steps; artifact storage and catalog UI are separate tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline ingests HF-style repo tarballs and S3 weight packages and emits a runtime artifact with stable hash and metadata.
- Automated conversion step produces CPU/GPU-compatible builds including INT8 candidate builds (when supported) and records kernel hints used.
- Validation suite runs: smoke generation, perf regression (vs baseline for similar architecture), deterministic token-level checks on held prompt sets, and safety filter baseline.
- Performance profile JSON is published to the model catalog with latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec) for target sequences [32, 128, 512], memory footprints, and cost-estimate inputs.
- Pin recommendation generated with primary pin (best latency/cost fit), fallback pins (quantized or lower-capacity variants), and rollout safety flags.
- End-to-end pipeline failures are surfaced to Slack channel #model-intake and create a tracked incident with reproducible artifacts.

Notes on non-goals: dataset evaluations for downstream tasks (e.g., summarization leaderboards) are out of scope; they will be handled by the Eval team integrations.
implementation_plan: 1) Intake adapters: extend artifact-gateway to support HF tar.gz with large-file streaming and signature verification (week 1). 2) Converter orchestration: containerized conversion runner that mounts weights, runs conversion toolchain (torch -> runtime tfm), records kernel profile, and emits candidate quant builds (week 2). 3) Deterministic validation: run smoke tests and token-diff harness; add held-prompt set for top-5 community models (week 2-3). 4) Microbench harness: spin ephemeral dedicated job to run seq-length/batch matrix; capture p50/p95/p99 and system metrics (week 3). 5) Pin logic: heuristic engine to compute primary/fallback pins and safety flags, store to model catalog service (week 4). 6) Observability: wire pipeline events to Console and Slack, add metric tags for model_id/version (ongoing).
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Initial spike for HF tarball streaming completed. Prototype adapter can stream a 6.2GB weights archive from S3 and compute a sha256 without full download. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/artifact-gateway/pull/314)

2026-02-20: Conversion runner container image prototype done. Uses conversion scripts from repo: github.com/redwood-inference/tools/convert. Early run converted a small 2B model and emitted runtime artifact. Observed discrepancy in kv-cache layout causing +12ms token latency — flagged for kernel hinting work.

2026-02-26: Deterministic token-diff harness wired to CI. Failing case on tokenizer special tokens normalization discovered; temporary workaround added to adapter to normalize BOS/EOS mapping. Unit tests added under tools/convert/tests.

2026-03-03: Microbench harness integrated with Dedicated staging pool. First profile run for sample Llama-variant shows p95 latency of 97ms @ seq=128 batch=1 on A100-40G using native kernels. Logged results to S3: s3://redwood-model-profiles/eng-63789/llama-sim/2026-03-03.json

2026-03-08: Pin recommendation heuristic v0.1 implemented. Rules: prefer unquantized if p95 < 80ms and cost delta < 1.3x; else recommend INT8 candidate if quality delta < 1% on token-diff. Added safety flag when tokenizer normalization fixes applied.
2026-03-11: Security review kickoff scheduled with Security team. Exported threat model and the conversion image SBOM to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-63789+SBOM
design_decisions: Use streaming ingestion + content-addressed storage (CAS) to avoid redundant full downloads; CAS keys recorded as model artifact stable IDs.
Conversion runner runs in isolated ephemeral containers with strict CPU/memory limits and KMS-managed access to weights. Keeps a signed provenance record for compliance.
Quantization: run candidate int8 pass but do not auto-pin int8 builds without token-diff & eval checks. Pin engine will surface int8 as a fallback unless explicit QA sign-off.
Performance profiling matrix is limited to seq=[32,128,512] x batch=[1,4,8] to keep job time reasonable while covering common production shapes.
Pin recommendation will provide human-readable rationale and a link to the full profile artifact for SRE/PM review before broad rollout.
Failures are deterministic and reproducible; pipeline will attach the converter logs, profile CSVs, and diff artifacts to failure tickets.
Security: conversion images must pass static scanning and have SBOMs. Secret material never persisted in artifacts (KMS-wrapped temporary creds only).
We will emit model metadata fields required by Console: model_id, version_hash, arch, param_count_estimate, tokenization_scheme, kernel_hints, profile_uri, recommended_pins.
Fallback routing: model catalog expects 1 primary pin and up to 3 fallback pins (quantized variants, smaller variant builds, or region-optimized copies).
risks_and_blockers: Kernel mismatch: conversion produced kernel choices that are not yet present in older runtime versions; requires runtime-side kernel negotiation support (tracking ENG-64201).
Quantization quality variance: some community weights produce catastrophic token diffs with INT8; we need a per-architecture threshold and, in those cases, avoid auto-pinning INT8.
SBOM & Compliance: Security needs time to review conversion images; block until SBOM checklist completed (security_review_required = true).
Storage costs for storing full microbench traces can grow quickly; need retention policy and an S3 lifecycle plan coordinated with Platform infra.
testing_and_metrics: Deterministic token-diff harness with acceptance threshold <= 0.5% token difference across held prompt set.
Performance SLOs: p95 < 120ms for target 2B-class models on Dedicated tier small pool; throughput measured in tokens/sec for seq=128 batch=1.
Quality metric: top-1 token mismatch rate and perplexity delta against golden sample set.
Operational metrics: conversion success rate, average conversion time, profile job failure rate, and time-to-publish-pin.
Alerting: create PagerDuty alert if conversion success rate < 90% over 24h or profile job queue latency > 30m.
